name: polylang
notes: DUO-3222 (version-pinned adapter compatibility contract): plugin/version_range verified live (not guessed) — polylang/polylang.php, re-confirmed at 3.8.6 this session (identical to DUO-3233's own sub_keys grounding and every other note below — same version, re-verified independently, not assumed stale-and-still-true). Range scoped to the CURRENT major line only (3.x, [3.0.0, 4.0.0)) — widening to cover other major versions is DUO-3224's ratification job, not invented here.

The engine capabilities this manifest depends on (docs/frontier/polylang.md's 'Proposed next task', task #20): (1) term-object relationship capture/apply — a term entity's own membership in OTHER taxonomies as object_id, symmetric to a post's `terms` field, filtered by each taxonomy's registered object_type exactly the way task #19's collision fix already filters post-side relationships. Needs NO manifest declaration at all (like category/post_tag need none today) — it activates the moment a term-object taxonomy is in site policy's `taxonomies` scope and registered at runtime. (2) `taxonomies.<tax>.description_refs`, declared below for the two taxonomies verified to need it.

Empirically verified on a fresh fx1/fx2 pair (Polylang 3.8.6, not guessed from the frontier report alone — re-checked byte-for-byte this session): `language` and `post_translations` are POST-object (`get_taxonomy()->object_type` = {"post":"post","page":"page","wp_block":"wp_block"} and ["post","page","wp_block"] respectively) — posts' existing `terms` field already round-trips these correctly, zero new code needed. `term_language` and `term_translations` are genuinely term-object (object_type === ["term"], confirmed) — every policy-scoped category (including Polylang's OWN auto-created 'Uncategorized-fr', created the moment a second language is added) gets term_language + term_translations relationship rows with ITSELF as object_id; these are what the new `relationships` term-file field captures. `language` and `term_language` do NOT share term rows for the same language (verified: English is term_id=2 under `language`, a DIFFERENT term_id=3 under `term_language`, with distinct slugs 'en' vs 'pll_en') — so there is no term-file-uuid-sharing hazard between the two taxonomies.

`taxonomies.post_translations.description_refs`/`taxonomies.term_translations.description_refs` (kind: post / term respectively): term_taxonomy.description on these two taxonomies' GROUP terms (Polylang's internal `pll_<hash>` bookkeeping terms) is PHP-serialized `{lang_slug: local_id}` — verified byte-for-byte this session: `a:2:{s:2:"en";i:1;s:2:"fr";i:2;}` for post_translations, `a:2:{s:2:"en";i:9;s:2:"fr";i:11;}` for term_translations — with GENUINELY int-typed values (`i:N;`, confirmed via raw DB read), never the ACF/Yoast digit-string convention, so no `cast` is declared. Rewritten via the ordinary json_refs primitive at path "$.*" (every top-level value in the flat map is a ref of the declared kind; the keys are language slugs, never ids, so no key_refs). WordPress never auto-unserializes term_taxonomy.description the way maybe_unserialize() does for postmeta/options — Capture/Apply explicitly unserialize()/serialize() it, the taxonomy-column analogue of _elementor_data's json_encoded handling but for PHP-serialize instead of JSON.

`language`'s OWN term description (NOT declared here) is a different, non-ref shape: `a:3:{s:6:"locale";s:5:"en_US";s:3:"rtl";b:0;s:9:"flag_code";s:0:"";}` — plugin config, no post/term ids, safe as the ordinary opaque tokenize_text() string every other taxonomy's description already gets. `term_language`'s own language terms (pll_en/pll_fr) have an EMPTY description ('', confirmed) — also nothing to declare. Declaring description_refs for either would be asserting a shape neither taxonomy has; Capture::term_description() throws loudly if a declared taxonomy's description doesn't unserialize to an array, so a wrong declaration fails fast rather than silently mis-capturing.

The `polylang` option (single blob, `force_lang`/`domains`/`hide_default`/`rewrite`/`redirect_lang`/`browser`/`media_support`/`post_types`/`taxonomies`/`sync`/`default_lang` authored config, `nav_menus` a per-location-per-language menu-term-id map, `first_activation`/`previous_version`/`version` env-local/upgrade-gate bookkeeping) is classified `env` as a WHOLE value (still correct: capturing it wholesale would let a stale `first_activation`/`version` silently roll back another environment's upgrade-routine gate) — CLOSED (DUO-3233): `post_types`/`taxonomies`/`nav_menus` are now carved out via the new `sub_keys` grammar below, capturing exactly those three keys and leaving every other key (including the env-local bookkeeping) untouched on every apply. This is the general sub-key option classification capability this note used to describe as 'a genuinely separate, unscoped engine capability ... deliberately not invented here' — it has since been built (see Policy::sub_keyed_options()/Apply::apply_option_sub_keys()) precisely for this option and Yoast's `wpseo` (identical shape). `post_types`/`taxonomies` are plain portable post-type/taxonomy-slug lists — no ref rewriting needed, a slug means the same thing on every environment (verified empirically, Polylang 3.8.6: `array_unique(array_merge(...))`-built values stay cleanly sequential-keyed, encoding as JSON arrays, not objects). `nav_menus[theme][location][lang] = menu_term_id` DOES need ref rewriting (a term id, local to its environment) — declared via the ordinary `json_refs` primitive at path `"$.*.*.*"` (three wildcard levels: theme, then location, then lang, landing on the term-id scalar — verified empirically against a real per-language menu assignment: `{"twentytwentyone":{"primary":{"en":9,"de":10}}}`), `kind: term` (a `nav_menu` term). This is a plain json_refs declaration, not option_ref_tokens' scalar/array `ref` mechanism (which cannot reach three levels deep) — so an unmapped id here follows json_refs' existing uniform warn-and-drop severity (spec/repo-format.md's 'Dangling references'), not task #73's unscoped-vs-dangling loud gate (which remains scoped to option_ref_tokens' own top-level `ref` mechanism and structurally cannot apply to a nested json_refs path — every other json_refs consumer in this codebase, e.g. wpseo_taxonomy_meta below, already behaves this same way).

`pll_language_from_content_available` and `pll_language_taxonomies` (classified `runtime`) are read from Polylang's own source (src/install/activate.php): both are `add_option()`'d ONCE at plugin activation — the former a UI-hint flag derived from whatever `force_lang` value existed at that moment (controls an admin-settings radio's available choices), the latter an empty operational cache — neither is content a site admin authors through any UI; both are installation-time artifacts of THIS environment's own activation history, not this site's config.

`polylang_wpml_strings` and `widget_polylang` (the classic Language-Switcher widget's instance storage) are deliberately left undeclared, not classified — both were empty in every verified fixture (`a:0:{}` and just the `_multiwidget` skeleton flag respectively), so their POPULATED shape (translatable strings registered via `pll_register_string()`; classic-widget display settings) was never empirically observed this session. Per this project's 'empirics over memory' posture, declaring either `authored` without having read a populated example would be exactly the kind of guess this manifest exists to avoid — left as a known, documented gap for whoever seeds a populated example next, the same treatment Yoast's manifest gives wpseo_rss/wpseo_internallinks/wpseo_xml.

Grind R3-A (task #90, docs/grind/r3a-multilingual-shop.md): confirmed live on Polylang 3.8.6 + WooCommerce 11.0.0 that description_refs/term-relationship capture (both capabilities above) work correctly on WOOCOMMERCE entities with ZERO new code — a translated product (post_translations), translated product_cat terms, and translated pa_color attribute terms (term_translations) all round-tripped correctly, resolving to each environment's OWN local ids on apply even where source/target ids genuinely differed. Also confirmed EMPIRICALLY, by reading src/settings/settings-cpt.php directly: free Polylang has NO license/Pro gate anywhere in the 'Custom post types and Taxonomies' settings module — marking a plugin-registered CPT/taxonomy (WooCommerce's `product`, `product_cat`, `pa_*`) as Polylang-managed is a free-tier mechanism, full stop; the commercial 'Polylang for WooCommerce' add-on's value-add is data SYNC (price/stock/gallery mirroring across translations) on top of this, not the base translation mechanism itself.

Grind round R3-A found two gaps sharing the same root cause (task #121): (1) the `polylang` option's `post_types`/`taxonomies` sub-arrays (which CPTs/taxonomies Polylang manages) are what actually gate whether `language`/`term_translations` relationships get WRITTEN for a managed CPT at all — on a fresh target that never had this admin setting replicated, `get_taxonomy('language')->object_type` simply never includes the managed type, so `pll_get_post_language()` reads false for every post of that type post-apply, independent of and unrelated to pa_*-style dynamic-taxonomy registration (task #92's separate scope). (2) the SAME option's `nav_menus[theme][location][lang]` sub-key (WP_Syntex\Polylang\Options\Business\Nav_Menus) is the ONLY mechanism that assigns a DIFFERENT menu per language to the same location — core.json's existing `nav_menu_locations` theme_mods capture is a completely separate, language-blind code path (one flat menu id per location, full stop; confirmed a plain `wp menu location assign` never touches the polylang option at all) — so a purpose-built second-language menu's own structure/items round-tripped correctly but the menu was never actually USED at its location on a fresh target. CLOSED (DUO-3233): both are the `sub_keys` declaration above. Verified live on a fresh pair (Polylang 3.8.6, own fixture CPT): a `project` CPT enabled for translation (`post_types` sub-key) and a translated pair resolve `pll_get_post_language()`/`pll_get_post_translations()` correctly on the target with zero manual Settings replication; a per-language menu pair assigned via the `nav_menus` sub-key renders the correct menu at its shared location per language (confirmed via real HTTP requests, both languages), with the term ids correctly re-mapped through the ledger to the target's OWN local ids.

One PHP-process-boundary timing nuance, discovered and precisely characterized while proving the above (not a sub_keys defect, not fixable by any code Duo's apply runs — WordPress's own register_taxonomy() fixes a taxonomy's object_type array once, for the ENTIRE process, at the `init` hook, which has already run before `wp duo apply`'s command body — and therefore before the SAME apply's own sub_keys merge — ever executes): on the apply run that FIRST writes `post_types`/`taxonomies` onto a fresh target, `language`'s object_type still reads its PRE-merge value for that entire process, so relationship-writing for any post of the newly-enabled type is skipped that SAME run, exactly like task #92's own pre-fix pa_* finding, and for the identical class of reason (a live registration snapshot the current apply request cannot itself update mid-run). The option write itself always lands correctly (confirmed directly against the database on every run) and takes effect starting the very NEXT wp-cli process, matching interplay finding on write-path reliability elsewhere in this file. What does NOT self-heal automatically, and is worth stating precisely: Apply's plan classifies a content-unchanged post as 'unchanged' (skips reprocessing entirely) or, once a later apply's snapshot reveals the live relationship is missing relative to what `duo_state` optimistically recorded, as 'drift (env ahead, untouched)' — and a drift-classified entity is BY DESIGN never touched again without an explicit human/tooling decision (spec/repo-format.md's capture-first bias), so a post that is never independently edited again will show persistent drift indefinitely. The proven, fully-automated remedy (confirmed live, zero manual Settings work either time) is the SAME playbook task #92's own report already established for pa_* attribute relationships: a genuine content change on the affected post(s), captured and re-applied, converges correctly — the realistic operator workflow when newly enabling an existing CPT for translation is to touch/re-save its existing content once, which Polylang's own documentation independently recommends for this exact scenario. Filed for the record, not attempted as a fix here — teaching Apply's own plan/drift model to force-reprocess entities affected by a same-run taxonomy-scope change is a materially larger, cross-cutting change belonging with task #92's own lineage, not this option-classification task.

A second, narrower, PRE-EXISTING and NOT-sub_keys-specific finding surfaced by the same testing: `wp duo lint`'s bare_id deep-scan for a json_refs-declared structure (`scan_structured_bare_ids()`) only flags an id-shaped VALUE sitting under an id-NAMED key (its `looks_like_id_key()` heuristic — e.g. wpseo_taxonomy_meta's own `wpseo-opengraph-image-id`). `nav_menus`' own shape keys its ids by LANGUAGE SLUG ('en'/'de'), which no safe id-naming heuristic could recognize (two-letter slugs are far too generic to add without mass false positives across every other json_refs consumer) — so an unrewritten nav_menus id would currently pass a lint audit silently, even though the rewrite mechanism itself (Tokens::struct_capture(), which rewrites by declared PATH, never by key-name matching) is completely unaffected and correctly declared either way. A blind spot in the audit-only detector, not in capture/apply. Filed for the record, not attempted as a fix here.

Also confirmed, a Polylang-plugin-behavior methodology note rather than a Duo gap: newly enabling a post type/taxonomy for translation (writing to the polylang option's post_types/taxonomies, whether via this same option shape a real admin's Settings-page save would write, or directly) does NOT reliably take effect for `pll_is_translated_post_type()`/`pll_is_translated_taxonomy()` — which read a cached list (`Model\{Post_Types,Taxonomies}::get_translated_object_types()`, backed by `PLL_Cache`, confirmed genuinely non-persistent/in-process-only by reading src/cache.php) — until Polylang itself is deactivated and reactivated. Confirmed stable afterward across multiple fresh wp-cli processes. Worth knowing before anyone else scripts a Polylang seed that enables translation for a non-default post type/taxonomy.

Polylang writes ZERO postmeta and ZERO termmeta (confirmed directly against a running install, matching the original frontier report) — its entire model is taxonomy- and option-based, so this manifest has no post_meta/term_meta sections and no meta_patterns.

No rebuilder is declared: Polylang free ships no wp-cli commands at all (`wp help pll` errors — confirmed in the frontier report and unchanged in 3.8.6), and this session's own testing found `pll_languages_list()`'s cache resilient to Duo's hook-free `$wpdb` writes (no rebuild/flush step needed after apply) — a deliberate absence, not an oversight.
